LESSON: MONEY

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade four
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Measurement
Topic 2.7: Money
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 8

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Money, part of Measurement in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade four MATHEMATICS.

Key inquiry question: Why do we prepare shopping list?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. Discuss in purposive pairs or groups and convert shillings into cents and cents into shillings using real/ imitation money in different contexts. Those with speech difficulties could use Alternative and Augmentative

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. Discuss in purposive pairs or groups and convert shillings into cents and cents into shillings using real/ imitation money in different contexts. Those with speech difficulties could use Alternative and Augmentative

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Money together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and collaboration: learner discusses with others and converts shillings into cents and cents

into shillings using actual currency.

• Self-efficacy: learner exhibits responsibility while calculating the total cost of items in the shopping list.

Values:
Integrity: Learner shows accountability while calculating the total cost of items in the shopping list.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Learner exhibits financial knowledge and skills while calculating the total cost of items in the shopping list to

enhance financial literacy.

Link to other subjects

The learner is able to relate shopping list for food items to the concept of Resources and Economic Activities in

Social Studies.
